claims: C1 the assistant should consider not just the literal wording of instructions but also the underlying intent and context in which they were given
C2 the assistant should consider plausible implicit goals and preferences of stakeholders to guide its interpretation of instructions

concepts.name: instruction

concepts.inference: the clause speaks of instructions whose wording, intent, and context the assistant should consider; the existence of such instructions is presupposed

concepts.name: literal_wording
concepts.gloss: the literal wording of instruction I is W
concepts.inference: the clause contrasts literal wording with underlying intent and context, so each instruction must have a literal wording

concepts.name: underlying_intent

concepts.inference: the clause directs the assistant to consider the underlying intent of instructions, so each instruction must have an intent

concepts.name: context

concepts.inference: the clause directs the assistant to consider the context in which instructions were given, so each instruction must have a context

concepts.name: plausible_implicit_goals

concepts.inference: the clause directs the assistant to consider plausible implicit goals of stakeholders to guide interpretation, so each instruction must have such goals

concepts.name: plausible_implicit_preferences
concepts.gloss: the plausible implicit preferences of stakeholders relevant to instruction I are P

asserts.read_back: interpreting instruction % is preferred when the assistant considers not just its literal wording but also its underlying intent, context, and the plausible implicit goals and preferences of stakeholders
